surfaces.part: gantry housing (ring face-on with display strip)

answer.evidence: The main body is the gantry, a tall face-on slab with a ring opening, a display strip at rows 5-6 and a base at rows 40-46. Its top (rows 1-4) is a flat front-facing strip with no front-edge line and no eave shadow, so it is not a top surface. The table at rows 22-28 reads as a thin side-profile slab, and the base block under it is a plain front face with only a 1-2 row light edge at rows 30-31. The silhouette widens from 22 to 47 px at rows 22-28 only because of the table. No major part shows a horizontal surface, so the drawing reads as front elevation.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's outline is a dark blue-grey that leans toward the neighbouring material, not neutral black. Measured neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, the same as the hedge and the cheese stall. Visible tones per 16x16 tile are 9, equal to the hedge and below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 11%, close to the stall's 13%, so there is no large dead fill. By eye, the white housing has a highlight, a mid tone and a shadow edge. The blue gantry ring has a bright inner glow and darker bands, and the bed and panel are separated by value. A machine casing is naturally smoother than wood or tile, so the 4 shading steps are acceptable, but it is a little thinner than the richest references. It would sit next to the references without looking like a flat sticker.

surfaces.part: gantry upper housing with display strip

answer.evidence: The main body is the gantry, rows 0-46 at width 22. It is a flat front panel with a ring drawn face-on. No horizontal top surface and no front-edge line with eave shadow appear at its top. Rows 1-4 are a plain light strip above the blue display on the same vertical face. The thin patient table (rows 22-28) has a narrow lit strip with a dark line below it, and the pedestal (rows 30-31) has a 2-row lighter band over a flat front. These are small parts, not the main volume. The whole object reads as a front elevation. It is also not a tall wall-standing furniture piece, so the kind fits poorly.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 9 visible tones per tile, the same as the hedge and well below the stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 11%, close to the stall's 13%. The dark edge pixels are tinted (0% neutral), so the outline is a dark blue-grey material tone rather than a black sticker line. The structure is still shallow: the white housing is only about 3-4 steps (white, light grey, mid grey, dark), with a large panel and side areas of near-uniform light fill. The bed/arm on the right is a flat grey slab with little grain. The blue gantry ring is the only part with real gradient, and it has no speckle, panel seams or per-surface texture like the references' tile scallops, plank grain or stone-by-stone shading. Next to the stall and well it looks thinner and flatter, with a smooth vector-like feel instead of the 5-6 step ramps and grain of Beodeul.
